patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports experiencing epigastric discomfort and cramping pain for the past 2 hours, noting that similar episodes have occurred in the past, mostly postprandially. patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Insignificant, except for chronic knee pain managed with over-the-counter painkillers.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with epigastric discomfort and cramping pain.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Doctor, for the past two hours I’ve had cramping epigastric pain and discomfort. It’s similar to episodes I’ve had before, mostly after I eat, and I’ve even lost some weight because I started avoiding meals to prevent the pain. I also smoke and drink alcohol only occasionally.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself needing to rush to the bathroom to urinate, even when your bladder doesn't feel completely full?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any urinary problems like feeling an urgent need to go, or trouble starting, and I don’t feel any bladder discomfort despite the symptoms being in my upper stomach.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any firm lumps or areas in your breast that feel different from the rest of your breast tissue?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any breast lumps or any areas that feel different from the rest of my breast tissue.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any small, firm bumps on your skin that are smooth to the touch?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any small firm bumps on my skin that feel smooth to the touch.”

turns.doctor_question: I've been reviewing your symptoms, and I wanted to ask: Have you been feeling like you can't seem to cool down or bring your body temperature back to normal, even when you're in a cool environment or not exerting yourself?
turns.patient_answer: Doctor, no—I haven’t had any trouble cooling down or keeping my body temperature normal, and I don’t feel overheated even when I’m not exerting myself.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling overwhelmed, anxious, or struggling to cope with your daily life lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t felt overwhelmed or particularly anxious, and my daily life has been mostly manageable, though I’ve been avoiding meals to prevent the pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching sensations on your skin lately, anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t had any itching sensations on my skin anywhere.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions on your arms, particularly along the veins?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions on my arms, and I don’t think anything looks different along the veins.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that it's been harder to find the right words when you're talking lately? Sometimes people have trouble thinking of the word they want to use, and it can be frustrating. Is that something you've been experiencing?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any trouble finding the right words or feeling like my thinking is slower when I talk.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any stiffness or tension in your muscles, like your muscles feeling really tight or hard to move, even when you're not trying to do anything physically demanding?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any stiffness or muscle tightness; my muscles feel normal and I’m able to move as usual. My main issue has been the cramping epigastric discomfort, mostly after eating.”

turns.doctor_question: How are you feeling today? Have you been feeling unusually sleepy or drowsy lately, or having trouble staying awake during the day?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I’m feeling uncomfortable from the cramping epigastric pain, but I haven’t been unusually sleepy or drowsy and I can stay awake normally during the day. My main problem is the discomfort after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: How are your legs feeling in terms of temperature? Do they feel warm to you?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, my legs feel normal in temperature to me—no unusual warmth and nothing feels markedly warmer than the rest of my body. The only thing bothering me is the cramping discomfort in my upper abdomen, especially after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you're coughing up mucus or phlegm, or is your cough mostly dry?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I don’t have a cough and I haven’t noticed any mucus or phlegm. My symptoms are mainly the cramping discomfort in my epigastric area, mostly after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rough, scaly patches on your skin recently?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any rough, scaly patches on my skin. My main issue has been the cramping epigastric discomfort that’s mostly triggered after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any skin lesions or rashes on your body that aren't painful or sensitive to the touch?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I haven’t noticed any skin lesions or rashes that are non-painful or sensitive to touch. My main problem is the cramping discomfort in my epigastric area, mostly after I eat.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you drink alcohol, or have you had any alcoholic beverages recently?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, yes—occasionally I drink alcohol, but I haven’t had any alcoholic beverages recently. The main issue is the cramping epigastric discomfort that started about two hours ago, mostly after I ate.”
